name: Vertical building shells and tenant improvements (per SF of gross building area)
notes: Building-only contractor price per gross SF incl. general conditions and contractor OH&P; EXCLUDES sitework (see site-work/paving/utilities blocks), structured parking, FF&E, land and soft costs. RLB figures (e1–e14) are hard construction cost per SF of gross floor area by metro in Q3 2026 dollars; RSMeans model pages (e15–e19) are 2019 national-average models whose 'Total Building Cost' includes a 7–8% architectural fee that is NOT part of our hard cost. Shell items carry a typical base-building interior fit (apartments are finished units; warehouse/PEMB/tilt-wall are shell-plus-minimal office).

items.name: Wood-frame low-rise building (1–3 stories, Type V; garden apartments, small commercial)

cost.method: RLB Q3 2026 multi-family LOW bounds for lower-cost metros (e1 Austin $190, e2 Dallas $195, e3 Phoenix $205, e4 Charlotte $220) bracket the garden/wood-frame end of the multi-family range. e15 RSMeans 2019 1–3 story apartment model = $164.48/SF open shop and $183.15/SF union after removing the 7% architectural fee (2019 dollars; build script escalates — not mixed into the 2026 range). Mid $190 = average of the four RLB low bounds ($202.5) less ~6% because RLB's 'low' still spans some podium product; low $150 = open-shop/low-cost-market garden product; high $240 = high-cost-market or upgraded-finish garden walk-up. Building only — no sitework or parking.

items.notes: Typical 2–3 story walk-up garden apartment or small wood-frame commercial building, finished. Use with quality multipliers in _common/adjustments.json.

items.name: Wood-frame mid-rise (4–5 stories Type III/V wood over a 1–2 story concrete podium)

cost.method: RLB Q3 2026 multi-family ranges for near-national metros (e1 Austin $190–285, e2 Dallas $195–285, e3 Phoenix $205–305, e4 Charlotte $220–375, e5 Denver $225–415, e6 Chicago $235–505). Podium/wrap product sits around the lower-middle of each range: mean of the four sunbelt range midpoints (Austin 237.5, Dallas 240, Phoenix 255, Charlotte 297.5) = $257.5, trimmed ~5% toward sunbelt product → mid $245; low $200 = sunbelt low bounds; high $310 ≈ Denver/Charlotte mid-range. e16 RSMeans 2019 4–7 story apartment = $174.26 open shop / $193.94 union incl. 7% A/E fee (2019 $, evidence only). Podium concrete is included; below-grade or above-grade structured parking beyond the podium is NOT (use parking block).

items.notes: 5-over-1 / 5-over-2 podium or wrap product, finished residential floors. Excludes structured parking decks.

items.name: Pre-engineered metal building (PEMB), erected and enclosed, light interior fit

cost.method: Derived — no direct PEMB $/SF source could be fetched this session. Anchored to RLB Q3 2026 warehouse ranges (e1 Austin $75–155, e2 Dallas $75–155, e3 Phoenix $85–170, e7 Chicago $155–245): a PEMB on slab with insulated metal panels is the cheapest enclosure in that class, so low $70 ≈ just under the sunbelt warehouse low bound, mid $105 ≈ 30th percentile of the sunbelt warehouse ranges, high $160 = upper warehouse range for a PEMB with masonry wainscot, mezzanine, HVAC'd office and higher eaves. Cross-check e19 RSMeans 2019 1-story CMU factory $115.78 open shop incl. A/E fee (2019 $). Verify with a metal building supplier + erector quote.

items.notes: Shop, warehouse, ag/equestrian, self-storage, sports barn. Includes slab, foundations, PEMB kit, erection, insulation, doors and basic MEP; excludes sitework, process equipment and HVAC beyond office areas.

items.name: Concrete tilt-wall warehouse / industrial shell (24–40 ft clear)

cost.method: RLB Q3 2026 Industrial-Warehouse ranges: e1 Austin $75–155, e2 Dallas $75–155, e3 Phoenix $85–170, e8 Charlotte $135–215, e9 Denver $140–225, e7 Chicago $155–245. Tilt-wall dominates big-box product in the sunbelt markets where most is built, so low $80 ≈ sunbelt low bound; mid $120 = mean of the six range midpoints ($155.4) weighted 2:1 toward the three sunbelt markets ($116–128); high $175 ≈ midpoint of the higher-cost markets. e17 RSMeans 2019 warehouse model = $119.27 open shop / $130.62 union after removing the 7% A/E fee (2019 $, evidence only). Shell incl. ~5% office build-out; full office/cold storage extra.

items.notes: Distribution / light-industrial shell with ESFR sprinklers allowance and dock pits. Dock equipment, racking and large office build-out are extra (TI items).

items.name: Concrete high-rise (8+ stories, Type I post-tensioned concrete frame)

cost.method: RLB Q3 2026 multi-family HIGH bounds represent Type I high-rise product: e3 Phoenix $305, e2 Dallas $285, e5 Denver $415, e6 Chicago $505, e10 Seattle $505, e11 New York $510, e12 Los Angeles $450, e13 San Francisco $700. Median of 18 US RLB high bounds = $430 (computed across all US metros in the table); mid set at $400 to temper luxury-coastal skew; low $300 = sunbelt high bound (Dallas/Phoenix); high $550 = Chicago/Seattle/NYC level (SF $700 is an outlier — regional factor covers it). e18 RSMeans 2019 8–24 story apartment model $205.08 open shop / $227.00 union incl. A/E fee (2019 $, evidence only; RSMeans national models run well below current RLB city data).

items.notes: Residential/hotel/office tower superstructure and enclosure with finished interiors at standard quality. Excludes below-grade parking and sitework.

items.name: Mass timber mid/high-rise (CLT/glulam, Type IV-A/B/C, 6–18 stories)

cost.method: Derived — no mass-timber cost study could be fetched this session. Positioned between building-wood-frame-mid (mid $245) and building-concrete-highrise (mid $400): mass timber competes with Type I concrete at 6–18 stories and is generally reported at rough cost parity to a modest premium for structure, offset by schedule. Mid $350 = average of the two comparables' mids ($322.5) + ~8% for exposed-timber finish quality, fire/acoustic topping and specialty erection; low $280 = 6–8 story Type IV-C in sunbelt; high $460 ≈ concrete high-rise upper-mid. Verify with a mass-timber supplier/CM preconstruction estimate.

items.notes: Includes CLT floors/roof, glulam frame, concrete topping, cores (often concrete) and finishes at standard quality. Excludes parking podium/below-grade.

items.name: Tenant improvement — basic / second-generation refresh (paint, carpet, minor partitions, MEP re-use)

cost.method: Derived from Cushman & Wakefield 2026 office fit-out guide: Gen 1 US average $162/SF (e20); Gen 2 adaptive reuse is a 10–15% discount (e22), i.e. ~$138–146/SF, but Gen 2 still builds a full corporate layout. A 'basic' refresh (re-use of ceilings, lighting and HVAC distribution; new finishes and limited partitions) is roughly half of Gen 1: mid $80 ≈ 0.5 × $162; low $45 = cosmetic paint/carpet only; high $120 ≈ just over the cheapest-market Gen 1 figure (e23 Kansas City/Cincinnati ≈ $108). Hard cost only; excludes furniture, IT/AV, soft costs.

items.notes: Office/retail/medical shell already conditioned; use for second-gen space or landlord vanilla-box refresh.

items.name: Tenant improvement — standard (Gen 1 corporate office fit-out, hard cost)

cost.method: Cushman & Wakefield Office Fit Out Cost Guide 2026: US average $162 psf for a Gen 1 fit-out (e20) = mid. Low $110 ≈ lowest US markets (e23 Kansas City $108.26, Cincinnati $108.03, Indianapolis $113.97). High $215 ≈ the gateway average $196 (e21) to Boston/NYC (e24 Boston $213.28, NYC ≈ $213). Hard cost only — C&W excludes furniture/FF&E, IT/AV and soft costs.

items.notes: Typical Gen 1 office fit-out incl. GC fee and contingency per C&W definition. Retail/medical TIs differ — medical runs higher.

items.name: Tenant improvement — high-end (premium finishes, heavy millwork, high density MEP)

cost.method: Derived. C&W 2026 reports market averages, not quality tiers: US avg $162 (e20), gateway avg $196 (e21), top markets San Francisco $228 / San Jose $224 / Seattle $223 (e25) and Boston $213 (e24). A premium-spec fit-out in an average market is assumed ≈ +45–50% over the US average Gen 1: mid $240 ≈ 1.48 × $162 (≈ top-market average); low $190 ≈ gateway average; high $320 ≈ 2× the US average for law-firm/trading-floor/executive spec. Hard cost only.

items.notes: Law firm, headquarters, high-end medical or hospitality-grade interiors.

items.name: Free-standing steel canopy (fuel island, drive-through, drop-off), incl. footings, fascia, lighting

cost.method: Derived — no fetchable canopy cost source this session. A canopy is roof + frame only (no walls, slab, interiors or HVAC), so it is priced as a fraction of the cheapest enclosed building: building-steel-preengineered mid $105/SF × ~0.6 ≈ $65 mid (frame, deck, drainage, caisson footings, LED lighting, fascia). Low $40 = simple PEMB-style canopy; high $100 = branded fascia/ACM, heavy wind/seismic footings, integrated signage. Verify with a canopy fabricator quote.

items.notes: Per SF of canopy plan area. Excludes paving below, fuel equipment and signage graphics.
